fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "How Music and Sky Began", "body": "Mike traced Music and Sky to an annual decompression gathering run by Burning Man friends in Los Angeles, which he said became a full festival when 2020 restrictions closed much of the larger scene. He described the Joshua Tree launch as sober, off grid and built around community, talks and workshops rather than headliners. Chance said he planned to attend. Mike said the October gathering in California capped near five hundred campers, served shared family dinners, hosted a children's village, and kept no backstage or VIP area. He also described a planned value for value membership platform and a workshop to certify local producers."}, {"title": "Sovereignty, Etymology, and Legal Language", "body": "Mike said the festival once carried a sovereignty label, and he defined the word as being master of your own domain. The speakers checked Webster's 1828 dictionary and talked through the French and Latin roots, and one speaker argued that living language shifts its meaning over time. Mike argued that if everyone is part of the creator, everyone is sovereign. Later Mike previewed an Alfa Vedic workshop on law and trusts, and Chance argued that the word maritime links etymologically to mort, the word for death, pointing listeners to Dylan Saccoccio's fourth book for the philology."}, {"title": "Counterculture From Punk to Festivals", "body": "Mike recalled 1990s underground raves and Orange County punk shows, and contrasted that era with what he called a far more conscious festival scene today. He said the West Coast festival circuit had grown saturated and corporate by 2020, and Chance argued that celebrity acts stand on pedestals built from advertising and marketing, which he called manufactured counterculture. When Gordy joined, he recalled seeing Bad Brains in Tucson in 1988 and said that show changed his life. Mike argued that musical scenes begin as authentic underground creation before outsiders co-opt them, and that people grow stronger when they come together."}, {"title": "Permaculture, Nature, and the Four Elements", "body": "Chance mentioned his recent interview with Matt Powers of permaculturestudent.com, and Mike said permaculture was a huge passion of his because it pairs human creativity with nature. Mike described a food forest he designed with seven layers, modeled on a forest but made edible, and said it was meant to bring the garden of Eden back. Chance observed that permaculture people share an unstoppable enthusiasm, and Mike answered that you have to love life. Later Mike said reading the Gospel of Peace convinced him that true health rests on four natural elements, sun, water, earth and fire."}, {"title": "Cosmology, Primary Water, and Falling Stars", "body": "Mike described a solo night on a mountain under the stars, and the speakers traded ideas about falling stars. Chance offered, as total speculation, that they might be beings descending from undifferentiated wholeness to incarnate, Mike suggested higher benevolent angelic hosts coming down to help, and Chance added that they could be chunks of the firmament. Mike also previewed a festival talk on primary water with Russell Anderson and a speaker he called Cosmic Sojourner, and argued that water is the consciousness of the realm and that fears of scarcity are misplaced. Chance added that solar and savior figures carry names tied to water and flow."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: DJ Mike Winner joins the Vibe Rant tonight! As co-host of the Alfa Vedic podcast with Dr. Barre Lando, Mike Winner is a voice of inspirational sanity leading us back to the wild and vivacious natural world. Tonight we'll talk about the upcoming Music And Sky Festival in California that Mike is putting on, this October!
